consequence.statement: When JMX is enabled, the JVM no longer gets an implicit IPv4 preference and uses its default IP stack preference instead; this lets clusters in IPv6-only environments boot correctly.
consequence.remediation: If your JMX setup relied on the IPv4 preference, check that JMX connectivity still works under the JVM defaults.

assertion.statement: In 0.46.0, Strimzi no longer adds an implicit IPv4 preference when JMX is enabled and uses the JVM defaults instead, so clusters can start correctly in IPv6-only environments.

proposal.undeterminedReason: applicability: The evidence says this applies 'when enabling JMX' but does not name the resource field or setting that enables JMX, so no exposure predicate can be written from the evidence alone.
